text:
maya: Heads-up — hit a weird bug in the Go sample app around generator streaming + auth retry. Repro is pretty simple and reliably dupes streams when token refresh happens mid-stream.

sam: Oh interesting. Steps to repro?

maya: 1) start sampleapp generator streaming with a long-running stream (e.g., < 1m)
2) during the stream, cause the access token to expire (I revoked it via local test KMS)
3) our transport does a 401->refresh->retry and the generator ends up emitting duplicate chunks from two concurrent streams.

sam: Yikes. Sounds like the retry wrapper is replaying the whole request instead of failing the stream. Can you paste the snippet?

maya: Here is the minimal pattern we're using in the sample:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.Generator(ctx).GenerateStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
defer resp.Close()
for chunk := range resp.Chunks() {
    // push to websocket / app
}
```
The problem: our HTTP transport retry layer catches 401 and reissues the request, creating a second in-flight generator. The original stream isn't properly canceled because cancellation lives on the outer context which the retry wrapper reuses.

ajay: Is this because the transport clones the request body and reuses the same ctx, so the inner stream handshake gets retried?

maya: Exactly. The retries are implemented at the RoundTripper level and don't distinguish streaming handshakes from idempotent calls. So when the long-poll handshake is retried you effectively get two live server-side sessions. Server sends tokens for both -> duplicates.

blake: Two quick mitigations: 1) make retries opt-in for streaming endpoints (fail fast on auth errors), or 2) ensure the retry logic attaches a new cancellable context per attempt and cancels previous attempts before retrying.

sam: We should also surface a Cancel/Close semantics in the Generator client that guarantees the transport will not implicitly retry the handshake after Close is called. Right now Close() only closes client-side readers, but the transport may still be mid-retry.

maya: I sketched a small change: expose GenerateStreamWithOptions(ctx, req, opts) where opts.DisableHandshakeRetry = true for long-lived streams. That way sampleapp can set it by default.

ajay: Can you open an issue + PR? I can review. This feels like an important DX bug for onboarding — users will see weird duplicated content and think generator is broken.

redwood-bot: Issue created: #2489 — "go: generator stream duplicate chunks when auth retry occurs" (assigned to maya).

maya: Thanks — will open PR with test + sampleapp change. Plan: update transport retry policy to skip handshake-level retries, add e2e repro test that simulates 401 mid-handshake, and mark sampleapp to set DisableHandshakeRetry=true for generator flows.

blake: Nice. Also add a short note in devex onboarding doc about "avoid credential rotation during active streams" until this lands.

maya: Agreed. Will drop a tiny blurb in the sampleapp README and the Go SDK streaming docs. Putting together the PR tonight, ping me if you want early look. :pray:

sam: Thanks — appreciate the quick triage and plan.

maya: One open question — should we try to make server-side idempotency for the handshake instead, so retries are safe? That is heavier but more robust.

ajay: Worth a separate RFC. For now do the client-side opt-out and docs. Server idempotency is a bigger contract.

maya: Cool. I'll proceed with the client + docs path.
